summary.name: OpenEmu
summary.one_liner: OpenEmu is an open source video game emulator frontend for macOS that organizes ROM backups into a unified library and runs them with multiple emulation cores.
use_cases: organize a personal ROM backup collection on a Mac
play retro console and arcade games on macOS
use a USB or Bluetooth gamepad with emulated games
browse game libraries with box art
summary.what_it_does: OpenEmu is a macOS application that combines several open source emulation projects into one interface. Users drag ROM backup files onto the app, which scans them and adds them to the matching console library with box art. It supports generic HID-compliant USB and Bluetooth game controllers, which it maps automatically for recognized devices. Users can create custom collections that mix games from different consoles. Emulation is provided by modular cores for a range of video game systems, though the page does not list them in the extracted text.
notable: Unified library that auto-organizes ROMs with box art
Modular cores from other open source emulation projects
Automatic controller mapping for generic HID USB and Bluetooth gamepads
Custom collections mixing games across consoles
caveats: Requires macOS; the minimum version is not filled in on the page (template placeholder).
Page says special instructions are needed for opening the app.
Games must be legally obtained ROM backups the user already owns; the app does not include games.
